Control Objective: Network security controls are defined, configured and maintained to protect the CDE.
Potential Evidence: Network diagrams, firewall/router rules, configuration standards, change tickets, rule reviews
Example Test Procedure: Compare current network/security-control configuration with approved data flows; inspect rule approvals and periodic reviews.
Notes: Selected mapping; applicability depends on scope.

Control Objective: System components are securely configured and default settings are managed.
Potential Evidence: Build standards, configuration exports, hardening checklists, vendor default review
Example Test Procedure: Sample in-scope components and compare configurations with approved secure baselines; inspect exceptions.

Control Objective: Stored account data is minimized, retained only as permitted, and protected in accordance with requirements.
Potential Evidence: Data-flow and data-discovery results, retention rules, encryption/key-management records, approved deletion evidence
Example Test Procedure: Verify whether account data is stored; inspect storage locations, retention and protection evidence. Never collect live PAN for this portfolio.
Notes: Sensitive authentication data storage is subject to strict PCI DSS prohibitions after authorization, even if encrypted, except narrowly defined permitted cases.

Control Objective: Strong cryptography protects account data during transmission over open, public networks where required.
Potential Evidence: TLS configuration, certificate inventory, approved crypto standards, scan results
Example Test Procedure: Inspect approved endpoints and TLS configuration; validate evidence against current applicable requirements and scope.
Notes: Exact testing criteria must be checked in the authoritative standard.

Control Objective: Malware prevention and detection controls are deployed and maintained as required.
Potential Evidence: Endpoint security coverage, alerts, update status, response records
Example Test Procedure: Compare in-scope system inventory with protection coverage; sample alert handling and update evidence.
Notes: Applicability depends on system types and requirement text.

Control Objective: Security vulnerabilities are identified and addressed; software and changes are developed and maintained securely.
Potential Evidence: Patch reports, vulnerability tickets, secure development procedures, code-review records, change approvals
Example Test Procedure: Sample vulnerabilities and changes from identification through remediation, approval and verification.
Notes: Include web-facing applications and relevant software lifecycle controls.

Control Objective: Access to system components and account data is restricted according to business need and least privilege.
Potential Evidence: Access matrix, role definitions, access requests, periodic access reviews
Example Test Procedure: Sample user and administrator access; compare effective access with approved job duties and review records.
Notes: Evaluate CDE access and relevant connected/impacting systems.

Control Objective: Users and administrators are uniquely identified and authenticated as required.
Potential Evidence: Identity inventory, authentication configuration, MFA evidence, access logs, joiner/mover/leaver records
Example Test Procedure: Inspect unique IDs and authentication/MFA enforcement for applicable access paths; sample account lifecycle events.
Notes: Validate all applicable requirements and exceptions against PCI DSS v4.0.1.

Control Objective: Physical access to facilities and systems in scope is controlled and monitored where applicable.
Potential Evidence: Facility access policy, visitor logs, badge review, media handling records
Example Test Procedure: Inspect physical access procedures and sample access/visitor records for relevant locations.
Notes: Applicability varies with hosting and physical responsibility model.

Control Objective: Access to system components and account data is logged, protected, reviewed and monitored as required.
Potential Evidence: Logging standard, log source inventory, time synchronization evidence, review records, alert tickets
Example Test Procedure: Trace selected events from source to protected log destination and review workflow; sample alert/incident records.
Notes: Verify retention, review frequency and event coverage against the standard.

Control Objective: Security systems and processes are tested as required to identify weaknesses and validate protection.
Potential Evidence: Vulnerability scans, penetration test reports, segmentation tests, IDS/IPS or detection test records
Example Test Procedure: Inspect test scope, qualifications, frequency, findings and remediation/retest evidence as applicable.
Notes: Testing frequency and conditions must be checked in the current standard.

Control Objective: Security policies, risk processes, awareness and service-provider oversight are maintained as required.
Potential Evidence: Approved policies, risk assessments, training records, incident response plan, service-provider register and agreements
Example Test Procedure: Sample policy approval/review, awareness completion, risk treatment and provider oversight evidence.
Notes: Map individual applicable sub-requirements during a real assessment.

Control Objective: Service providers are identified and managed, and their relevant compliance status and responsibilities are monitored.
Potential Evidence: Provider inventory, contracts, responsibility matrix, current AOC and service scope, annual review records
Example Test Procedure: Confirm provider services and responsibility split; check that evidence is current and covers the relevant service.
Notes: The provider's evidence does not replace assessment of merchant responsibilities.

Control Objective: Incident response is prepared and implemented for relevant security incidents.
Potential Evidence: Incident response plan, contact list, tabletop exercise, incident records, lessons learned
Example Test Procedure: Inspect plan approval and test evidence; verify actions and ownership from a tabletop or actual incident where authorized.
Notes: Check exact sub-requirement applicability in the authoritative standard.

Control Objective: Where segmentation is used to reduce scope, it is configured and tested to isolate the CDE as intended.
Potential Evidence: Approved scope diagram, segmentation rules, test plan and results, change records
Example Test Procedure: Review segmentation design and inspect evidence that prohibited paths are blocked and the test scope/frequency meets applicable requirements.
Notes: Segmentation does not automatically remove connected systems from scope; validate with the assessor/acquirer.
